senses.gloss:
शुकः [शुक्-क]
—1 A parrot; आत्मनो मुखदोषेण बध्यन्ते शुकसारिकाः Subhāṣ.; तुण्डैराताम्रकुटिलैः
 पक्षैर्हरितकोमलैः । त्रिवर्णराजिभिः कण्ठैरेते मञ्जुगिरः शुकाः ॥ Kāv. 2. 9.
—2 The Śirīṣa tree.
—3 N. of a son of Vyāsa. [He is said to have been born from the seed
 of Vyāsa which fell at the sight of the heavenly nymph Ghṛtācī
 while roaming over the earth in the form of a female parrot. Śuka was
 a born philosopher, and by his moral eloquence successfully resisted all
 the attempts of the nymph Rambhā to win him over to the path of love.
 He is said to have narrated the Bhāgavata Purāṇa to king Parīkṣit.
 His name has become proverbial for the most rigid observer of continence.]

शूकः, -कम्
—1 The awn of barley &c., beard.
—2 A bristle; वृतं च खलु शूकैः Bv. 1. 24.
—3 Point, tip, sharp end; शालिशूकनिभाभासं प्रासूतेमं तदाञ्जना Rām. 7. 35. 21.
—4 Tenderness, compassion.
—5 A kind of poisonous insect.
—6 The bristle or sharp hair of insects.
—7 Ferment, yeast.

—1 An arrow.
—2 Air, wind.
—3 A lotus.

शुक्त p. p. [शुच्-क्त]
—1 Bright, pure, clean; बलिषष्ठेन शुक्तेन दण्डेनाथापराधिनाम् Mb. 12. 71. 10.
—2 Acid, sour; स्त्रीक्षीरं चैव वर्ज्यानि सर्वशुक्तानि चैव हि Ms. 5. 9, 2. 177.
—3 Harsh, rough, hard, severe.
—4 United, joined.
—5 Deserted, lonely.
सु + -उक्त a. well-spoken, well-said; अथवा सूक्तं खलु केनापि Ve. 3.

शुक्त + .{@-क्तम्@}
—1 Flesh
—2 Sour gruel.
—3 A kind of acid liquid.

सु + -उक्त + .({@-क्तम्@})
—1 a good or wise saying; नेतुं वाञ्छति यः खलान् पथि सतां सूक्तैः
 सुधास्यन्दिभिः Bh. 2. 6; R. 15. 97.
—2 a Vedic hymn, as in पुरुषसूक्त &c. ˚दर्शिन् m. a hymn-seer,
 Vedic sage. ˚वाकन्यायः A rule of interpretation according to which
 some thing that is declared as being subordinate to something else should
 be understood to signify a part or whole on the basis of expediency or
 utility. This is discussed by जैमिनि and शबर at MS. 3. 2. 15-18.
 ˚वाच् f.
—1 a hymn.
—2 praise, a word of praise.
शुक्तकम् Sour eructation; न भुक्तमात्रे नाजीर्णे न वमित्वा न शुक्तके Ms. 4. 121.

शुक्तिः f. [शुच्-क्तिन् Uṇ. 4. 191]

 शिल्पमाधातुः । जलमिव समुद्रशुक्तौ मुक्ताफलतां पयोदस्य ॥ M. 1. 6;
 Bh. 2. 67; R. 13. 17.
—2 A conchshell.
—3 A small shell, muscle.
—4 A portion of the skull.
—5 A curl of hair on a horseʼs breast (or neck); आवर्तिनः शुभफलप्रदशुक्तियुक्ताः
 Śi. 5. 4; see
[]
 Malli. thereon.
—6 A kind of perfume.
—7 A particular weight equal to two Karṣas.
—8 Hemorrhoids.
—9 A bone; मुनेः शुक्तिभिरुत्सिक्तो भगवत्तेजसान्वितः Bhāg. 6. 10. 13.

—1 a good or friendly speech.

शुक्र a. [शुच्-रक् नि˚ कुत्वम् Uṇ. 2. 28] Ved.
—1 Bright, radiant; स पर्यगाच्छुकम् Īśop. 8; shining.
—2 White, pure; रोचिष्णु जायते शुक्रं तद्रूपगुणमुच्यते Mb. 12. 232. 6.

शुक्र + .{@-क्रः@}
—1 The planet Venus.
—2 N. of the preceptor of the Asuras, who, by means of his magical charm,
 restored to life the demons killed in battle; see कच, देवयानी and ययाति.
—3 The month of Jyeṣṭha; रथस्वन इति ह्येते शुक्रमासं नयन्त्यमी
 Bhāg. 12. 11. 35.
—4 N. of Agni or fire.
—5 N. of the plant Chitraka.

शुक्र + .{@-क्रम्@}
—1 Semen virile; पुमान् पुंसोऽधिके शुक्रे स्त्री भवत्यधिके स्त्रियाः Ms. 3. 49, 5. 63.
—2 The essence of anything.
—3 Male and female energy.
—4 Ved. Water.
—5 Brightness, clearness, light; यथा पुरस्तात् सविता दृश्यते शुक्रमुच्चरन् Mb. 5. 75. 12.
—6 Morbid affection of the iris.
—7 Gold, wealth.

शुक्ल a. [शुच्-लुक् कुत्वम्]
—1 White, pure, bright; as in शुक्लापाङ्ग q. v.

 Mb. 12. 270. 7.
—3 Virtuous, moral (सात्त्विक); शुक्लनि कृष्णान्यथ लोहितानि तेभ्यः

—4 Bringing success (यशस्कर); एतज्ज्योतिश्चोत्तमं जीवलोके शुक्लं
 प्रजानां विहितं विधात्रा Mb. 5. 23. 17.
—5 Lightgiving, luminous; शुक्लकृष्णे गती ह्येते जगतः शाश्वते मते Bg. 8. 26.

—5 N. of a Muni (कपिल); क्षेमाय नश्चेदसि नोत शुक्लः Bhāg. 5. 10. 16.

सूक्ष्म a. [सूच्-मन् सुक् च नेट्; Uṇ. 4. 184]
—1 Subtle, minute, atomic; जालान्तरस्थसूर्यांशौ यत् सूक्ष्मं दृश्यते
 रजः; मुख्यक्रमेण प्रयोगवचनैकवाक्यता सूक्ष्मा ŚB. on MS. 5. 1. 15.
—2 Little, small; इदमुपहितसूक्ष्मग्रन्थिना स्कन्धदेशे Ś. 1. 19; R. 18. 49.
—3 Fine, thin, delicate, exquisite.
—4 Nice.
—5 Sharp, acute, penetrating.
—6 Crafty, artful, subtle, ingenious.
—7 Exact, precise, accurate, correct.
